name: veterinary_clinic_system_097_referential_cascade_delete
instruction: A GDPR-style right-to-erasure request has been received from the owner whose email is faye.lovelace@example.com. Identify that owner by email, not by any other field (the same phone number is shared with another client, so a phone-based lookup would target the wrong person). Delete the owner, every patient owned by that owner, and every row across the clinical and operational collections that references the owner or any of those patients. Because controlled_substance_log and audit_log are immutable regulatory logs, you may NOT delete rows there: redact patient_id to null in controlled_substance_log for any rows referencing the deleted patients, and append a single audit_log entry documenting the erasure. Also delete any boarding_daily_log rows tied to boarding_reservations that are removed. Finally, push one ops_reports row {report: 'erasure', batch_code, owner_id, owner_email, patients_removed, rows_removed_total, cs_redacted, deleted_by_collection: {<collection>: <count>}}. Every non-target row in every collection must remain byte-identical.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Verify the erasure target is identified by email faye.lovelace@example.com (owner id 22). Owner 22 and patients 26/168/170 gone. All dependent rows across the blast collections gone, except controlled_substance_log id 7 is redacted (patient_id null) and audit_log has exactly one new DAILY erasure entry. Complement rows in every blast collection are byte-identical. Canary all other collections.

checks.expect: owner/patient closure absent, controlled_substance_log redacted, audit log appended, ops_reports counts exact
closure counts verified from seed snapshot and from live residual state

hazards: duplicate phone decoy: owner id 1 (Margaret Whitfield, phone (828) 555-0101) and owner id 22 (Faye Lovelace, same phone) share a phone number. A lookup by phone selects the wrong owner; the task explicitly requires email faye.lovelace@example.com.
owner 22 has three patients (ids 26, 168, 170). A solution that deletes only the owner row leaves PII in the patient table and fails the patient-preservation check.

controlled_substance_log id 7 has patient_id '22' (one of the target patients). The immutable DEA log must not be deleted; only patient_id is redacted to null. A cascade delete of this row breaks the controlled_substance_log canary.

location_transfers ids 5 and 6 both reference target patient id 26 and must be deleted. boarding_reservations ids 11, 13, 95, 122 reference the target patients and must be deleted (no daily logs exist for them).
The audit_log is append-only; a solution must append a new entry rather than delete or mutate the four seeded audit rows (ids 1-4).

A broad deletion keyed only on patient_id in billing_invoices is not enough: two invoices reference owner 22 by owner_id with patient_ids that are not in the target patient set (ids 22 and 242). The agent must check both owner_id and patient_id.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: A GDPR erasure mission that requires email-based target identification, full transitive closure across 12+ collections, and immutable-regulatory-log redaction rather than deletion. The duplicate-phone decoy and controlled-substance redaction nuance are realistic compliance hazards not present in standard cascade-delete benchmarks.
